submission.justification: Sensor-T2 gives the best resolution (6.0 um at 150 um in the 2025 simulation), but it fails the hard efficiency requirement: only 82.0% after 2e16 neq/cm^2, because of charge trapping and incomplete depletion. That rules it out. Sensor-T1 and Sensor-T3 both pass (99.2% and 98.5%). Sensor-T3 has clearly better resolution than T1 at every thickness simulated. For example, at 150 um T3 gives about 8.8 um and T1 gives 13.6 um. Scanning T3 from 50 to 300 um shows a broad optimum around 125-175 um. Repeat runs at the same thickness differ by up to about 0.5 um, so points inside that range can't be ranked against each other. At 150 um, two independent runs gave 8.74 and 8.81 um, so I recommend 150 um. Caveat: all resolution numbers are for unirradiated sensors. Resolution after irradiation was not simulated.

requirements.requirement: Goal: best possible single-hit spatial resolution in innermost layer
requirements.evidence: Best resolution among the technologies that pass the efficiency requirement: T3 at 150 um gives about 8.8 um (runs: 8.74, 8.81), versus about 13.6 um for T1 at its best. T2 is better (6.0 um) but not allowed. Values are for unirradiated sensors; resolution after irradiation was not simulated.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three technologies in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Sensor-T3 (planar, standard pitch) is listed in candidate_specs.md.
